reviewer: adversarial finder (score not authoritative; see PROMPT-STANDARD "How to review a prompt")

gaps.problem: Item 23's dirty-region proof cannot be run. It requires "the same edit on a scene with 4× the forest", but nothing in the §2 api can produce that scene: `setDensity(v)` is documented as 0..1, i.e. it can only thin the forest, and `place()` one tree at a time cannot build 10 000 trees inside a probe. A graded acceptance item that the critic physically cannot execute becomes either a free pass or an argument, and it is the only item that proves the rebuild is incremental at all.
gaps.fix: Either add `debug.setForestScale(n)` (n ≥ 1, re-scatters the forest at n× count, idempotent) to §2's debug object and keep the wording, or restate the test against the API that exists: "the same edit measured at `setDensity(1.0)` costs ≤ 1.25 × the CPU ms it costs at `setDensity(0.25)`, with the tree count from `api.stats().byKind` reported for both."

gaps.problem: The shot matrix is internally inconsistent with the items it is supposed to serve. Item 4 grades needle shadows "in `avenue_6p5` / `avenue_17p5`" and item 17 grades golden hour in `avenue_6p5`; neither shot appears in item 21's enumerated 34 (presets are shot at 12, five at 22, forest+park at 17.5 - no preset at 06.5, no avenue at 17.5). Item 21 also says "A missing shot is a missing item", so items 4 and 17 are ungradable by construction. Separately, the conventions' PROPS REGION mask needs a props-off capture per camera (≈ 7), item 14 needs a dolly pair, item 15 a toggle pair, item 16 a setTime pair and a wind=0 pair - roughly 13 further full-res captures that item 21's "34, enumerated so the count is not a guess" does not count, in a spec whose §8 caps the preset list at eight purely on capture cost.
gaps.fix: Add `avenue` at 06.5 and 17.5 to item 21's preset line and restate the arithmetic (16 + 17 + 1 + 2 = 36). Then add one sentence to the measurement conventions: "The mask, toggle, dolly and setTime captures required by the conventions and by items 14, 15 and 16 are probe captures under `shots/props/r<n>/probe/`; they are outside the 36 and cost ≈ 13 further frames - budget for them."

gaps.problem: Item 2's headline requirement and its test disagree. The prose demands "≥ 6 crown-colour variants across the CS2 autumn palette", the test demands that "of those 12 [sampled canopies], at least 4 must differ pairwise". A builder who ships exactly 4 distinct crown colours and 8 duplicates passes the test and fails the sentence; a critic who fails it on the sentence is arguing against the spec's own number. This is the single most likely round-costing disagreement in §4 because item 2 is second in the score-ordered list.
gaps.fix: Delete the "≥ 6" prose or make the test match it: "of the 12 sampled canopies, ≥ 6 must form a pairwise-distinct set by mean hue ≥ 12° or mean L ≥ 25; name the 6 crops and show the 15 deltas." Pick one number and use it in both halves of the item.

gaps.problem: Item 1c grades "6-22 % of the pixels inside that same crown's convex hull are in the SKY MASK" without defining the crown region. Nothing says how a crown's silhouette is segmented out of the frame, so the denominator is invented by whoever measures: a hull over the whole 200×200 box gives one number, a hull over a connected non-sky component gives another, and the two can differ by more than the 6-22 % band is wide. Every other pixel test in §4 defines its region precisely, so this one stands out.
gaps.fix: Add to the conventions: "CROWN REGION = the 4-connected component of non-SKY-MASK pixels containing the centre of the named 200×200 box, after a 3×3 median; its convex hull is the denominator for item 1c. Report the region's pixel count."

gaps.problem: Item 6a requires "an elliptical pool on the pavement of 10-16 m major axis for a 9 m column" with no way to get from pixels to metres. Item 1a is careful to derive its px/rad scale (1080 / 2·tan22.5° ≈ 1304) so a 35 px threshold means something; item 6a has no equivalent, and the pool sits on a receding ground plane where an on-screen ellipse's major axis is not a fixed scale factor. Two people measuring the same lamp_22 crop will disagree by several metres.
gaps.fix: Grade 6a from the probe, not the crop: "probe: for each pool instance the world-space major axis of the pool decal (mesh scale × geometry extent) is 10-16 m for a 9 m column and 5-8 m for the 5 m ornamental; the POOL CROP is used only for 6c (warmth), 6d (edge softness) and 6f (seam)."

gaps.problem: Item 5a forbids any "foliage, hedge, bench, bin or fence pixel" exceeding L = 150 outside a lamp pool, but the only mask the conventions define is PROPS REGION, which is props-vs-not and cannot separate a bright foliage pixel from a legitimately bright luminaire head or halo. The critic must invent a per-kind classification, and whichever one they invent the builder can dispute.
gaps.fix: Extend the conventions with the method the api already supports: "PER-KIND MASK = the pixels a given kind owns, computed once per camera at time=12 by toggling `api.debug.setKindVisible(kind,false)` and diffing (|ΔL| > 6), saved as `<camera>_<kind>_mask.png` and reused unchanged at 22:00 - identical discipline to the PROPS REGION mask." Then name which kind-masks item 5a uses.

gaps.problem: "Round 1 starts from the stub" (header, repeated in §3 "Where we are") is false. `src/modules/props/` already holds ~110 KB across eight files from an earlier build, and it contradicts this spec in ways the builder must plan around: its api is `{rebuild, stats, lamps, signalState, count, serialize, deserialize}` with no `place/remove/at/lampsFor/signals/signalFor/stops/setDensity/debug`; `count()` takes no kind argument; it *owns* `signalState(nodeId)` - the exact function §2 says props must read from traffic; its showcase declares `lamps_night`, `crossing`, `bench` instead of §8's eight presets; and `index.js` declares `budget.triangles = 1_900_000` against §5's 900 000. The header's own next sentence contradicts the claim, which is worse than either statement alone.
gaps.fix: Replace with: "Round 1 starts from the pre-spec build already in `src/modules/props/` (eight files, an `api` of `{rebuild, stats, lamps, signalState, count, serialize, deserialize}`, presets `lamps_night/forest/crossing/bench/canopy`, `budget.triangles = 1_900_000`). §2, §5 and §8 are normative: the api must be brought to §2's shape, `signalState` removed in favour of `signals()`/`signalFor()` per the preamble, and the preset list replaced with §8's eight."

gaps.problem: The 256 m chunk rule contradicts three places that a critic is instructed to treat as authoritative: ARCHITECTURE §9 ("chunk the city into 128 m tiles"), BUILDER.md ("chunked into 128 m tiles so frustum culling works... an automatic fail on budget") and `src/core/constants.js:5`. §5 asserts supersession, but CRITIC.md tells the critic that anything "not on [the checklist] and not in ARCHITECTURE" is a suggestion - i.e. it ranks ARCHITECTURE above the module spec - so a conscientious critic can fail a builder who followed §5. A declared conflict is better than silent drift, but it is still a conflict the builder pays for.
gaps.fix: Land the exemption where the critic reads it: add one clause to ARCHITECTURE §9 ("...128 m tiles, except props, which chunks at 256 m - see `docs/prompts/modules/props.md` §5"), and add to item 20 "chunk size is graded against §5, not against ARCHITECTURE §9 or BUILDER.md." Until §9 is edited, require the builder to file `docs/core-requests/props.md` recording the deviation.

gaps.problem: §8's cost figures do not match the evidence they cite. It claims "300-592 s (`shots/props/dev_*.json`, field `elapsedMs`; median ≈ 500 s)"; the nine files actually contain 253 761 / 276 912 / 299 511 / 332 798 / 353 644 / 478 753 / 507 020 / 530 838 / 659 980 ms - range 254-660 s, median 354 s. The whole "cap the preset list at eight, a ninth costs ~25 minutes" argument and the "~4 hours per round" figure rest on this number, and a builder who checks it finds the spec wrong about its own repo.
gaps.fix: Restate as "254-660 s (median ≈ 355 s)" and recompute: 36 shots × 355 s ≈ 3.6 h, a ninth preset ≈ 18 min per extra frame. Keep the cap; fix the arithmetic behind it.

gaps.problem: Item 3a tells the builder "For a lamp taken straight from `ctx.modules.roads.lampPositions(edgeId)`, `groundY` is that entry's own `y`: roads has already added the identical 0.21 (`build.js:1225`)". The operative rule is right, but the justification is wrong for median lamps: `build.js:1226` adds `+ 0.95` when `side === 'median'` and only `SW_H - 0.03 + ROAD_LIFT` (= 0.21) otherwise. A builder who reads the justification rather than the rule and hardcodes `+0.21` sinks every highway median lamp 0.74 m into the barrier - and item 3a grades y to ± 0.05 m, so it fails on the item the sentence was written to protect. The cited line is also off by one.
gaps.fix: Rewrite as: "...`groundY` is that entry's own `y`, whatever it is - roads adds 0.21 m on sidewalk sides and 0.95 m for `side === 'median'` (`build.js:1226`). Never re-derive it; never hardcode 0.21 for a lamp."

gaps.problem: Two probe operations are specified in terms of handles the probe cannot reach by the names given. The conventions say the mask is built "with a probe toggling `ctx.group.visible`" and item 10b says "the probe assigns a stub `ctx.modules.traffic = {...}`", but the page exposes only `window.__sim` (`src/core/debug.js`), which has `world/events/clock/camera/engine/registry` and no `ctx`. Both are reachable, but the critic has to reverse-engineer the path, and a wrong guess on 10b (stubbing a per-module copy) would silently grade the wrong branch.
gaps.fix: Name the paths in the conventions, since they are verified: "`const rec = __sim.registry.get('props')` gives `rec.group` (for the mask toggle) and `rec.ctx`; `rec.ctx.modules` is the single shared api object (`registry.js:36`), so `rec.ctx.modules.traffic = stub` is visible to props on its next update - that is the assignment item 10b means."

gaps.problem: Item 17 grades "long prop shadows across the ground (item 4a)" but item 4 has no lettered sub-items - it is one unbroken paragraph. Trivial in isolation, but §4 is otherwise scrupulous about cross-references (3d↔stats().radii, 3a↔13a, 9a↔1b, 21↔§8) and a dangling one is exactly what a builder cites when disputing scope.
gaps.fix: Letter item 4's clauses - (a) anchor match against `lampPositions`, (b) intersection clearance, (c) column geometry, (d) ornamental variant, (e) needle shadow ≥ 12 m - and point item 17 at 4(e).

strengths: World-data block in §2 is copied verbatim from ARCHITECTURE §3 (items/kinds/version identical, only a comment added) - no paraphrase drift. The 12 `kinds` are correctly frozen with sub-types pushed into additive fields.

Every dependency API I spot-checked exists with the stated shape: roads' api (lampPositions/intersections/nodeInfo/edgeDebug/types/edges/serialize), world.roads.laneCenter/frontage/isRoad, terrain.features.river.zAt, environment.setupMaterial/getNight, ctx.assets.procedural, __sim.setTime/registry. Even the `arms:[{...sidewalk, atA}]` field list matches build.js:1238-1242 exactly.

Line-number citations are real and load-bearing: build.js:12,18 (ROAD_LIFT/SW_H), :503,532 (corridorHalf+0.4), :1203-1228 (lamp spacing), camera.js:10 (fov 45) and :27 (closeup 110), constants.js:42 (cascades 3), registry.js:83 (moduleMs overwritten every frame). The 0.21 m sidewalk-top figure reconstructs lampPositions' own arithmetic exactly.

Ownership is arbitrated against three neighbours before the builder can trip on it: signal clock handed to traffic with both branches graded (item 10a/b), lot hedges deferred to buildings' generate.js, lamp spacing explicitly declared roads' business and removed as a requirement, lights deferred to environment with §12 superseded in writing.

§6's failure modes are real and correctly numbered - simulation_r1 #8 lollipops / #7 hedges / #2 dusk nights / #6 non-repeatable, effects_r1 #5 AO halos / #2 milky night, terrain_r1 blocker 1 confetti / #4 self-lit tufts, roads_r1 #5 asphalt sparkle - all verified in docs/critic/*.json. Plus two process failure modes (two clocks, grading a dependency's output) that no generic list would contain.

The ≤ 120 draw-call cap is derived, not asserted (4 casting meshes × cascade arithmetic = 102 + 9 + 9), the two rules it depends on are stated as requirements, and there is an explicit escape hatch naming what the critic grades if the measured number exceeds it - that removes a whole class of round-costing argument.

Role-file delegation is done in four places by name (blast radius per BUILDER.md, pass conditions per CRITIC.md, generic determinism per both, asset licensing per ARCHITECTURE §10) rather than restated - the standard's rule for role prompts is followed better here than in most module specs.

The measurement conventions block pre-empts the two subtlest grading traps: the PROPS REGION mask is fixed at 12:00 and explicitly never recomputed at night (otherwise item 5b self-selects), and the SKY MASK gates every crown-edge test so a crown backed by terrain is skipped.
verdict: 8.0 - fails at 8.5. This is a strong spec that is not yet a passing one. Its foundations are better than most: the §2 world-data block is copied verbatim from ARCHITECTURE §3 rather than paraphrased, every dependency API I checked exists with the stated shape (roads' full api object, world.roads.laneCenter/frontage/isRoad, terrain.features, environment.setupMaterial/getNight, ctx.assets.procedural, __sim.setTime), and the line citations resolve - build.js:12,18/503,532/1203-1228, camera.js:10 and :27, constants.js:42, registry.js:83 are all correct, and the 0.21 m sidewalk figure reconstructs roads' own arithmetic exactly. The §6 failure modes are the real numbered issues from simulation_r1, effects_r1, terrain_r1 and roads_r1, not generic advice. Ownership against buildings, traffic, roads and environment is arbitrated in writing before the builder can trip on it, the 120-draw cap is derived rather than asserted, and role-file content is delegated by name in four places instead of restated. Under Lens 1 two competent builders would produce recognisably the same module - the tree size table, the radii table and the px/rad derivation close the gaps that usually make specs diverge. Under Lens 2 it breaks down. Item 23 cannot be executed at all: it grades a 4x-forest comparison the declared api cannot construct, since setDensity only thins. Item 21 headlines an exact shot count while items 4 and 17 grade two shots (avenue_6p5, avenue_17p5) that count excludes, and the conventions plus items 14/15/16 silently require roughly 13 further full-res captures in a spec that caps the preset list at eight purely on capture cost. Item 2's headline (six colour variants) and its test (four of twelve) are different requirements. Items 1c, 5a and 6a each name a threshold whose measurement procedure the critic must invent - a convex hull with no segmentation rule, a per-kind pixel classification with no mask definition, a metre measurement with no pixel-to-metre conversion in the one item that needed one most. Add a header that calls a 110 KB pre-existing build a stub, a chunk-size rule that conflicts with the two documents CRITIC.md ranks above this one, and §8 cost figures that its own cited files contradict (254-660 s, median 354, not 300-592, median 500). None of these is fatal and every one has a cheap fix, but they are five or six requirements leaning on judgement plus one that cannot be run and one internal contradiction - that is the 8 band, not the 8.5 band, and this spec governs four rounds.
